chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the milks of camels, cattle, and sheep, and their urine and their meat. He said: Do not perform wudu (ablution) from it, and if anything from it reaches you or a garment of yours, then do not wash it, except that you do so for cleanliness.

He said: And I asked him about the urine of riding animals, mules, and donkeys. He said: Wash it. If you do not know its place, then wash the entire garment. And if you doubt, then sprinkle water over it.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِهَا: their urine; referring to the urine of camels, cattle, and sheep
key_terms.اغْسِلْهَا: wash it; an instruction to cleanse the impurity
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment or clothing affected by the substance mentioned
key_terms.فَانْضَحْهُ: sprinkle it; apply water by sprinkling in the case of doubt
key_terms.لَا تَتَوَضَّأْ: do not perform wudu (ablution); here meaning it is not used for ritual purification
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ: its place; the specific spot of impurity on the garment

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about the urine of livestock, mules, and donkeys regarding purity and washing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the purity status of substances from certain animals. It distinguishes between the urine of camels, cattle, and sheep, and the urine of riding animals, mules, and donkeys, explaining when washing a garment is or is not required.
